LESSON: CHEMICAL FAMILIES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Matter and Chemical Reactions
Topic 2.2: Chemical Families
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Chemical Families, part of Matter and Chemical Reactions in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How are elements suited for their use in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Chemical Families together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: as the learner carries out activities to investigate the reaction of sodium, magnesium and chlorine with air

and dilute acids.

● Digital literacy: as the learner uses available digital devices with assistive technology to carry out research on transition

elements and their uses.

Values:
35

Love: as the learner takes care of self and others by observing safety when carrying out activities to investigate properties of

elements of the periodic table and appropriately using first aid kits in case of injuries.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Socio Economic and environmental issues - Safety and security: as the learner takes precautions when reacting different

elements with acids.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Metals such as sodium, magnesium, copper, iron, zinc, lead,

● Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers and screen magnifiers,

● Print and tactile braille version of the periodic table,

● 3-D models of the periodic table,

● Print textbooks in appropriate font and colour,

Braille textbooks.

Investigating the physical and chemical properties of selected elements of the periodic table.
